issues.description: The problem statement requires that class Bitmap24 has a constructor accepting three parameters: width, height and a background color (as char). However both the template and the solution only declare and define two constructors: a default constructor and a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height). There is no three-parameter constructor declared in the header or implemented in the .cpp. This mismatch will confuse students: the specification asks for a 3-argument constructor but the provided header does not expose such a constructor to implement/override, and the reference solution does not demonstrate the intended signature/behavior.

The problem statement requires the class Bitmap24 to provide a constructor that accepts three parameters: width, height and a background colour (as char). However both the template and the solution repositories only declare/implement a two-parameter constructor Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height) (and a default constructor). This is an API/signature mismatch: students are told to implement/expect a 3-parameter constructor but the starter code and reference code expose only a 2-parameter signature. This will confuse students (which constructor to implement/use), may cause compile errors or unnecessary edits to unrelated code (e.g. main), and increases extraneous cognitive load when mapping the requirement to the provided code.
issues.suggested_fix:
Align the code with the problem statement by providing a constructor that accepts (int width, int height, char background). To minimize disruption, add an overloaded constructor rather than replacing the existing one:

- In Bitmap24.hpp add a prototype: Bitmap24(int i_width, int i_height, char i_bg);
- In Bitmap24.cpp implement Bitmap24::Bitmap24(int p_width, int p_height, char p_bg) to allocate data = new char[width*height*3]; and initialize every pixel triplet to p_bg (or to an appropriate RGB triplet derived from p_bg), or interpret the single char as desired and document it. Keep the existing two-parameter constructor as-is (or implement it to call the three-parameter one with a default background value) so existing code paths (e.g. resize_buffer usage) remain valid.

Alternatively, if the intended requirement was only two parameters, update the problem statement to require a two-parameter constructor. Prefer the first option (adding a 3-parameter overload) because it preserves the stated exercise requirement and avoids forcing students to change multiple files.
